public.diagnosis: The still prompt names a 'blank gold nameplate' among the desk objects. A nameplate exists to carry a name, so the image model engraved lettering on it, and 'blank' is a negation the model ignores — that is the still gate's refusal, twice. The same prompt names a 'blank post-it note array' (post-its exist to carry writing) and keeps a monitor in frame while asking for 'abstract glow', so the model drew colourful square content on the left monitor; and it puts Sarah's folded hands inside a chest-up frame, where the clip morphed them. The picture itself invites all three defects, so the still is described again and the clip is made from the new picture.

observations: The still rewrite moves Kael's pose and gaze into one short standalone clause before the desk and room detail, states the framing once as a single with the subject facing the viewer, describes the headset plainly with no brand, and replaces the writing-bearing desk objects with objects whose purpose needs no writing — the picture-side causes of the same defect are addressed even though the findings are logged on the motion layer.

The motion prompt still keeps the fixed sentence 'No subtitles, no on-screen text.', which names the forbidden thing; the added clause 'the middle of the frame clear and open' gives the model something positive to fill that space with, which is the treatment available on this layer.
The ending frame in the motion prompt names no camera move and stays a visible description, so it survives the composer's ending rule.
